transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t seem to stop worrying. It feels like it’s everything at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, house projects I keep dropping… and I keep thinking I’m basically failing as a husband and father.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying, even when you try to stop or calm it down?

Yes. I try to stop it, but it doesn’t really shut off. Like at work I’ll tell myself, just focus on the code in front of you, but then one worry grabs onto another. Before I know it, I’m imagining a bad review turning into losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. Even when I’m working out and trying to breathe through it, my mind keeps going.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind and feel intrusive or hard to dismiss?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like random images or anything, but worries keep pushing their way in. Even if I tell myself to just focus on the code in front of me, or I try to breathe through a workout, one concern hooks into another. Then I’m way ahead in my head, imagining a bad review turning into losing my job, and my family being worse off because of me.
Did these worries start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

I don’t think it was one single event, exactly. It’s been about nine months now. It seemed to start when the cloud migration at work really ramped up, and around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular.
Do you feel driven to do anything over and over—like checking, counting, repeating, or seeking reassurance—to relieve the worry?

I don’t think so. I mean, I might check things if I’m worried, but I don’t feel like I have to count or repeat something a certain way to make the worry go away. It’s more that the worry just keeps running in my head.
Do your worries feel mostly centered on the problems at work and the conflict at home, or do they also show up a lot in other parts of your life?

It’s not just work and home conflict, no. Those are big parts of it, but it spreads out. I worry about bills, stuff around the house I keep not finishing, whether I’m letting my kids down, whether I’m failing as a husband and a father. It kind of feels like everything piles on at once and I can’t shut it off.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I feel depressed most days, exactly. I feel worn down and overwhelmed a lot, but I haven’t really thought of it as being “down” in that way.
Do you feel your anxiety would mostly go away if the problems at work and the conflict at home improved?

Probably not completely. I mean, if work got better and things at home calmed down, I’m sure that would help. But I came in because I can’t stop worrying about everything at once—my marriage, whether I’m slipping at work, bills, the house stuff I keep dropping, and whether I’m just failing as a husband and father. It feels bigger than just one problem.
For the past 6 months or more, have you been worrying like this on most days?
Yeah. I’d say it’s been about nine months now, most days. It really started when the cloud migration at work ramped up, and around the same time the arguments at home started becoming more regular.
Lately, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
Not most of the day, no. I get worn out and kind of discouraged sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m sad all day or down most of the day.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Yes. I feel wound tight almost all day, like my shoulders are locked up and I’m bracing for something. I’ll catch myself pacing between meetings, or at chess club I’m tapping the pieces because sitting still just feels really hard.
Do you often feel tired easily?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do get tired, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s unusually easy or more than normal.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind is occupied by worry?

Yes, definitely. At work during sprint planning or code reviews, I’ll read the same design note three or four times and still miss things. It’s like part of my brain is busy running through what I might’ve forgotten at home, or worrying about how the next argument is going to go, so I’m not fully taking in what’s in front of me.
For the past two years, have you felt depressed or down most days?
I’m not sure I’d say most days for two years. I’ve had down days, but I haven’t really tracked it that way. It’s not something I can clearly answer yes to.
Do you often feel muscle tension?

Yes. I feel wound tight most of the day. My shoulders are kind of locked up, like I’m bracing for something. And I notice I pace between meetings or tap pieces when I’m at chess club because sitting still just feels hard.
Have you been feeling more irritable than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed being more irritable than usual in a clear way. I mean, I can get annoyed like anyone, but I can’t say it’s been a big change.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes. Most nights I’m exhausted when I get into bed, but my mind just keeps going — work risks, money, stuff I said to my wife. And if I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 and then I’m already thinking through tomorrow’s problems, so I can’t really get back to sleep.
Has this worrying been causing problems in your work, home life, or daily functioning?

Yes, it’s definitely causing problems. At work, my manager has started writing down missed architectural details in my designs, which is not like me. And at home, I keep leaving projects half-finished, and I’m so distracted that arguments with my wife keep getting worse.
